title: 1980 AHSME Problem 19
statement: Let \(C_1,\) \(C_2,\) and \(C_3\) be three parallel chords of a circle on the same side of the center. The distance between \(C_1\) and \(C_2\) is the same as the distance between \(C_2\) and \(C_3.\) The lengths of the chords are \(20,\) \(16,\) and \(8.\) The radius of the circle is

answerChoices.label: E
answerChoices.text: not uniquely determined by the given information

solutions.text:
Let \(r\) be the radius, \(u\) the distance to the \(20\)-unit chord, and \(v\) the common spacing. Then \[ \begin{aligned} r^2&=u^2+10^2,\\ r^2&=(u+v)^2+8^2,\\ r^2&=(u+2v)^2+4^2. \end{aligned} \] Consecutive subtraction gives \(2uv+v^2=36\) and \(2uv+3v^2=48,\) so \(v^2=6\) and \(u=\frac{15}{\sqrt6}.\) Hence \[ r^2=u^2+100=\frac{275}{2}, \] and \(r=\frac{5\sqrt{22}}{2}.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is D.
hints: A perpendicular from the center bisects each chord
Let the nearest chord be distance \(u\) from the center and the common spacing be \(v\)
